title: Guardian: end-to-end onboarding pipeline for community LLMs with pinning and profile publishing
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Build a hardened end-to-end pipeline (Guardian) to onboard community/open-source LLM weights into Redwood's artifact catalog, create runtime-ready conversions, run deterministic validation and performance profiling, and automatically produce a recommended pin + performance profile for publishing. Goal: reduce manual triage for new models, raise quality bar for runtime compatibility, and shorten time-to-publish from days to hours for typical OSS models. This ticket covers orchestration, conversion hooks, smoke and deterministic validation suites, profiling matrix generation, and the pin-recommendation algorithm. Excludes UI work in the Console (separate PM ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Weights ingest supports signed manifests and provenance metadata and rejects malformed or missing required fields
Conversion path produces runtime artifacts (quantized and FP16 candidates) with artifact checksums and deterministic outputs for canonical smoke inputs
Validation harness runs unit smoke tests + deterministic seq-level equality for supported ops on CPU/GPU/quantized paths
Profiling job emits a per-model performance matrix (latency P50/P95, memory, KV growth) across target accelerators and sequence length buckets
Automatic pin recommendation returns a stable model pin and candidate fallback variants with rationale (throughput, latency, memory)
Telemetry and alerts populate Console dashboards: ingest failures, conversion errors, profile regressions, and pin-rejection rate
End-to-end can be executed by CI with a sample OSS model and produces an artifact bundle and a profile JSON ready for publish
approach_summary: Implement an orchestrator service (stateless coordinator + per-model worker pods) that sequences artifact ingestion -> conversion -> deterministic validation -> profiling -> pin-recommendation -> publish staging. Use containerized conversion steps with hermetic toolchains (transformers patch, model schema validation, quantization hints). Store intermediate artifacts in artifact store with versioned prefixes and immutable pins. Leverage existing runtime kernels for profiling harness and extend kernel selection telemetry to emit per-step timings.
design_tradeoffs_and_notes: We prefer hermetic conversion containers to minimize environment drift; this increases operational overhead but reduces intermittent conversion failures
Deterministic seq-level equality is expensive; we'll limit full equality to a canonical set of inputs and use probabilistic sampling for broader coverage
Aggressive auto-pinning could publish suboptimal variants; the pin recommender will always propose a primary plus 2 fallbacks and requires human approval for P0 customers
We will initially focus on CPU, CUDA-A100, and ML accelerator X64; adding narrowly used accelerators later to avoid explosion of profiling cost
test_plan: Unit tests for manifest parser and schema validator
Integration test: ingest -> convert -> smoke -> profile for a small transformer (eg. community-bert-small) in CI
Deterministic regression suite comparing converted artifact outputs with reference outputs stored in test fixtures
Load test: orchestrator must handle 10 parallel small-model conversions without increased failure rate
Chaos test: simulate S3 latency spikes and ensure orchestrator retries do not cause duplicate publishes
rollout_and_migration: Phase 1 (internal): run Guardian in staging with manual gating; publish profiles to a staging catalog namespace
Phase 2 (beta): enable auto-pinning for non-production customers with an opt-in flag and collect metrics for 2 weeks
Phase 3 (general availability): enable for all OSS model onboarding with default automation and Console visibility
Backout strategy: all publishes to main catalog are soft (staged tag) until manual promotion; automated publishes can be rolled back by revoking pin and reverting to previous pin
metrics_to_monitor: Median time from ingest -> published profile
Conversion failure rate per model type
Profile variance (differences between staging and runtime measures)
Pin accept rate (auto vs manual) and subsequent regression incidents
open_questions: Should we run quantized profiling on CPU for both int8 and int4 candidates or defer int4 until runtime experiment?
What's the expected SLA for ingest-to-profile for enterprise customers (we currently propose <24h by default)?
How will licensing and provenance requirements affect acceptance criteria for community weights with custom licenses?
Do we require model fingerprinting + reproducible seed artifacts for all community uploads?
deliverables: Guardian orchestrator service and k8s deployment manifests
Hermetic conversion container images and publicly documented conversion tool spec
Deterministic validation harness and canonical input fixtures
Profiling runner with accelerator matrix output and Console ingestion hook
Pin recommendation module with scoring and rationale fields
Automated telemetry dashboards and alert rules in Console
Documentation: Confluence onboarding runbook and operator playbook
